questions.question: Which documentation entry is most objective and useful?
choices: Client is doing poorly and seems noncompliant
Client is probably developing an infection
1415: respiratory rate 28, speaking in short phrases, temperature 38.5°C; provider notified
Client was difficult all afternoon
questions.explanation: The entry gives time-stamped, observable findings and communication without judgment or unsupported diagnosis. Objective documentation enables other clinicians to identify the change, see what action occurred, and continue safe follow-up.

questions.question: Which statement belongs in the Background portion of an SBAR call?
choices: I am calling because the client is newly short of breath
The client has a history of heart failure, received IV fluids today, and was speaking comfortably one hour ago
I think the client may be in trouble
Please come to the bedside now
questions.explanation: Background supplies relevant history, recent events, baseline, and treatments that explain the current concern. The immediate problem belongs in Situation, focused findings are Assessment, and the needed action belongs in the Recommendation or Request.

questions.question: A provider gives a new verbal instruction that the RN cannot clearly hear. What should the RN do?
choices: Guess the most likely instruction and implement it
Use the required read-back or check-back process to clarify and confirm the instruction
Wait until the next shift to see whether it was charted
Ask another client what they heard
questions.explanation: Unclear instructions must be clarified using the organization’s read-back or check-back process. Repeating the information back for confirmation reduces communication error and ensures the RN understands the intended action before implementation.

questions.question: Which handover detail has the highest priority to communicate to the oncoming nurse?
choices: A stable chronic symptom already described in the care plan
A new drop in blood pressure, pending provider response, and the timing of the next reassessment
A routine hygiene task planned for later in the shift
A completed test with normal results and no pending action
questions.explanation: A new blood-pressure change, pending response, and follow-up timing directly affect safety and continuity. Handover prioritizes changes, risks, treatments, and tasks that the next clinician must recognize and act on.

questions.question: The RN realizes a charted entry contains an error. What is the appropriate action?
choices: Delete the entry so no one can see it
Use the approved correction process and preserve record integrity according to policy
Ask a coworker to change the entry under their name
Ignore the error because the next note will be accurate
questions.explanation: Health records must remain accurate and traceable. The RN uses the approved correction process rather than erasing, concealing, or asking another person to alter the record, then documents relevant current information as needed.

questions.question: Which action best protects client privacy when documenting electronically?
choices: Open any record on the unit to learn from it
Access only records needed for care, secure the screen, and use approved accounts and devices
Share a screenshot in a group chat without names
Leave a workstation unlocked for the next staff member
questions.explanation: Electronic records are accessed only for a legitimate care purpose through approved, secure systems. Protecting screens, accounts, and client information supports privacy and record integrity; removing a name from an informal screenshot does not make sharing appropriate.

questions.question: After an RN reports new confusion and hypotension, the provider says, “Just keep watching.” What is the priority concern?
choices: The RN should assume the vague response is a complete plan
The response may be insufficiently clear for a potentially deteriorating client and requires clarification and escalation
The RN should document only that the provider was called
The RN should wait for routine morning rounds before reassessing
questions.explanation: A potentially unstable client needs a clear, actionable plan. The RN clarifies the request or recommendation, communicates objective concerns, follows escalation pathways when needed, and continues reassessment rather than treating an ambiguous response as adequate.

questions.question: Which action shows that an urgent communication loop has been closed?
choices: The RN left a message but did not check for a response
The RN gave SBAR, confirmed the response, completed required actions, reassessed the client, and documented the outcome
The RN added a vague note at the end of the shift
The RN assumed the next nurse would see the monitor alarm
questions.explanation: Communication is complete only when the message is received and understood, the needed action is carried out, and the client’s response is evaluated and documented. A message alone does not ensure continuity or demonstrate that risk was addressed.

questions.question: Which client statement should be documented as a direct quote because it describes a new concern?
choices: The client is anxious
The client states, “This is the worst chest pressure I have ever felt.”
The client is exaggerating symptoms
The client seems worried about tests
questions.explanation: A direct quote preserves the client’s own description of a potentially urgent symptom without interpretation. The RN also performs immediate focused assessment and follows the required escalation process; documentation never replaces urgent action.

questions.question: Which handover practice best supports safe continuity of care?
choices: Recite every historic chart entry without prioritizing
Share current status, recent changes, risks, therapies and equipment, pending tasks, goals, and required follow-up
Avoid questions so the report ends quickly
Discuss client details in a public elevator after leaving the unit
questions.explanation: Safe handover is concise but complete about information the next clinician needs to continue care, including changes, risks, equipment, pending tasks, and follow-up. Questions and clarification are part of reliable communication and privacy remains essential.
